sections.h2: Can a Paterson house be sold without waiting on a listing?
sections.html:
A cash offer on a house left in its current state skips repairs and showings, while a listing or direct sale takes more time. Paterson adds its own layers for vacant buildings, rent leveling and certificates of occupancy, so learn which ones apply before you choose a route.

Owners live in just 26.9 percent of Paterson's homes, so sellers often hold small rental buildings or inherited the property. Start with this checklist:

  • Confirm whether the property counts as vacant, which triggers a city registration.
  • Find out if tenants live there and whether the building is covered by the rent leveling ordinance.
  • Collect the deed, the payoff figure and any code violation notices.
  • Ask the Division of Community Improvements what inspection a change of occupancy needs.

Paterson is Passaic County's seat and its largest municipality, with 161,793 residents in the 2025 estimate on 8.41 square miles of land. It has 49,865 households, and renters hold most of the housing. The median owned home is valued at $360,100, typical rent is $1,548 and median household income is $55,997.

The Passaic River runs through the city. In August 2011 Hurricane Irene pushed it to levels unseen in about a century, so a riverside seller should prepare an honest flood answer before a buyer asks. Neighborhood demand changes from ward to ward, so price against recent sales on your own street. Ask your agent or attorney which comparable sales are closest to your block, and be ready to explain any open code items.

sections.h2: Vacant, foreclosed and rental property rules
sections.html:
Building, electrical, plumbing and fire inspectors enforce the state construction code in Paterson. They issue permits and final approvals, including Certificates of Occupancy and Continued Certificates of Occupancy. Inspections, licenses, permits and certificates of occupancy all run through the Division of Community Improvements, which posts weekday hours on its construction code page. Call 973-321-1232 to find out what your sale requires.

Paterson registration rules
Property situationRegistration deadlineCost
Vacant buildingWithin 30 days of becoming vacant or of taking ownership$2,000 a year
Foreclosed propertyWithin seven days of the creditor starting foreclosure$500 a year
Covered rental under rent levelingWithin 30 days of receiving the annual formNo fee

A vacant building owner names a local agent aged 21 or older who can be reached at all hours. Once a vacant property is sold or transferred, the owner gives the city proof within 30 days. Rent leveling registration is filed under Chapter 381 of the municipal code.

sections.h2: When Paterson calls a property abandoned
sections.html:
A property can be deemed abandoned once it has gone six months without legal occupancy and meets another test: no rehabilitation, stalled construction, an unpaid and delinquent tax installment, or a nuisance finding by the public officer. Inspectors look for boarded windows, disconnected utilities, piled-up mail and overgrown yards when they decide a building is vacant.

Check with the Division of Community Improvements whether your house has been flagged before you sign a contract. A flag can affect the fees you owe and what the buyer will want settled at the table.

If you are inheriting or taking over a house that has sat empty, sort out the registration first. The 30-day clock starts when you take ownership, and a buyer's attorney will ask for proof that it was filed.

sections.h2: What to have ready for a Paterson sale
sections.html:
Most delays in Paterson come from paperwork that was never started. Before you accept an offer, pull together the deed, your mortgage payoff figure and every code violation notice you have received. Note the dates of any registration filings for a vacant or foreclosed building, since the buyer's attorney will ask for proof.

If the building is a rental, find the annual rent leveling registration form and confirm it was returned within 30 days of receipt. Tenants in place stay in place, so the buyer inherits the leveling rules along with the leases. Give the buyer's side copies of leases and security deposit records early.

When the house is vacant, expect questions about utilities, boarded windows and the local agent named on the registration. Fixing those before listing keeps the city from treating the property as abandoned and keeps the closing calendar clear.

sections.h2: Realty transfer fee and state forms
sections.html:
Trenton sets the Realty Transfer Fee, and the seller pays it. Rates climb in bands from $2.90 up to $6.05 per $500 for prices above $350,000, and from $2.00 up to $3.90 per $500 for prices at or below that line. Your closing attorney can give you the exact dollar amount for your price.

Sellers who are seniors, blind or disabled pay reduced bands, and the claim is made on a form recorded with the deed. An estate deed to an heir is exempt. A GIT/REP form is recorded too, signed by whoever signs the deed, so the State can tell whether a seller from another state must prepay income tax.

Flood answers are required as well. Since March 20, 2024, the disclosure statement has to state the FEMA flood zone and any known flooding before the buyer signs. The DEP Flood Risk Notification Tool can help you look up your lot.

sections.h2: How can I appeal Paterson property taxes?
sections.html:
Appeals go to the Passaic County Board of Taxation, and the petition must be in its hands by April 1. After a citywide revaluation or reassessment the date is May 1.

Show that the assessment misses market value or falls outside the district's common level range, which is 15 percent either side of the average ratio. Property assessed above $1,000,000 can skip to the State Tax Court, and a county board ruling can be taken to that court within 45 days. Your balance comes from the Paterson tax collector. File before you list if you think the assessment is high, because a pending appeal is something a buyer will ask about.

sections.h2: Steps for selling a Paterson house for cash
sections.html:
Cash suits a building with code problems, tenants you no longer want to manage, or a vacancy registration piling up at $2,000 a year. The buyer takes the property in its present state, which removes the repair list and the showing schedule.

The city's paperwork still applies. Work through it in this order:

  1. Call the Division of Community Improvements and ask what a change of occupancy needs for your address.
  2. Register the building if it counts as vacant, and confirm any rent leveling registration is current.
  3. Gather the deed, the payoff figure and any code violation notices for the buyer's attorney.
  4. Agree in writing on who orders inspections and who pays any reinspection.

Some sellers also use a cash sale to end a vacancy registration that renews every year. Compare offers by what you net after payoff, the seller's transfer fee and the months a listing could take. Where tenants are in place, ask how leases and deposits will be handled before you sign.

faqs.q: Must I register a vacant Paterson house?
faqs.a: Yes, when it fits the city's definition of a vacant building. Registration is due within 30 days, with a $2,000 yearly fee.

faqs.q: How does Paterson treat foreclosed properties?
faqs.a: The creditor that files the foreclosure complaint registers the property within seven days, at $500 for the first year and each renewal.

faqs.q: Which office issues certificates of occupancy in Paterson?
faqs.a: The Division of Community Improvements, which enforces the Uniform Construction Code. Its construction code page posts weekday office hours.

faqs.q: Does the seller cover the state transfer fee in Paterson?
faqs.a: Yes. The State bills the seller at recording, in bands that rise with the price.

faqs.q: What is the Paterson tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1, or May 1 after a revaluation, at the Passaic County Board of Taxation.
